designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch the fixed ring and the producer write position. Then, thinking ahead to several consumers each seeing every value, sketch what extra state each consumer needs and what 'the buffer is full' means when they read at different speeds. Name the shared storage and the per-consumer cursor.

parts.title: SPSC push/pop

hints.text: A fixed array plus two positions is enough for one producer and one consumer. How do you tell full from empty?
Store a write counter that never wraps, and a read counter on the consumer. Unread is write - read. Full when that equals capacity. Slot index is counter % capacity.

slots = [None]*capacity, write = 0. register_consumer() makes a Consumer with read = write. push stores at write % cap and increments write if write-read < cap. pop returns slots[read % cap] and increments read.

probes: How do you tell full from empty when both can leave head == tail if the counters wrap?
Which indices are shared between producer and consumer in SPSC?

parts.title: Broadcast to many consumers

hints.text: Each consumer needs its own idea of 'how far have I read.' What is full if they disagree?
One ring, many read counters. push is full when the *largest* unread among consumers equals capacity. A fast pop does not free a slot a slow consumer still needs.

Keep a list of Consumer objects each holding read. push: if max(write - c.read for c in consumers) >= capacity: False. Else write the slot and increment write. Each pop only advances that consumer's read.

probes: SPSC first, then SPMC — which indices became per-consumer, and which stayed shared?
Why is a private queue per consumer the wrong default, even though it broadcasts?

parts.title: Late join and unregister

hints.text: A consumer created after two pushes should not magically know those two values. Where should its read cursor start?
Late join: read = current write (empty until the next push). Unregister: that cursor no longer participates in the max-unread full check.

register_consumer() already does read = write if you set it at construction. unregister sets a dead flag (or removes from the list); push with no live consumers raises, same as part 1 with zero registrations.

probes: Power-of-two capacity masking versus `%` — when does it matter?
(discussion) cache lines and false sharing on the producer write counter versus per-consumer reads

criteria: broadcast exact; full determined by the slowest live consumer
one shared ring plus cursors, not a private copy-queue per consumer
late join is a cursor initialised to write, not a replay of history
monotonic read/write counters with modulo only at indexing
slow-consumer-full and late-join edge cases considered before being told
stated which indices are shared and what 'full' means with multiple consumers
